summary: Client TCP delayed-ack / zero-window leads to WebSocket chat stream silence mid-generation
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that long-streaming chat sessions using WebSocket stall mid-generation and stop receiving tokens for 20-40s before either resuming or terminating with a socket error. Impact: Multiple production endpoints for NovaHealth's clinical chat feature are affected; patients see partial replies or timeouts leading to degraded experience. Environment: Dedicated instance in prod-us-east backing NovaHealth (dedicated capacity, pinned model open-llm/medassist-13b-v1).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Open websocket to /v1/chat/stream with Authorization header and session metadata. 2) Send a prompt that triggers a long response (~1200-2200 tokens). 3) Observe initial tokens stream for ~5-30s then an extended silence (20-40s). 4) Client either receives a socket close (ECONNRESET) or resumes after delay with a burst of tokens. Reproducible from behind customer NATs and certain corp proxies; not reliably reproducible from developer laptops.
observed_behavior: SSE/WebSocket connection remains open on our side but no additional token chunks are written for the duration of the silence. No consistent 5xx from gateway. Client-side TCP stack shows zero-window or delayed-ack activity during silent periods in packet captures provided by customer.
expected_behavior: Tokens should stream continuously (subject to normal model generation pacing) without long silent gaps. Connection should not hit application-level stalls due to network-level delayed ACKs.

initial_triage_notes: Customer packet captures show repeated TCP zero-window advertisements and delayed ACKs coming from the customer's NAT device or corporate gateway. Our proxy observed socket send buffer exhaustion (socket_buf_free=0) during stalls. Hypothesis: client-side slow ACKs cause kernel TCP flow control which in turn starves our application write loop because we rely on kernel to accept writes; when socket buffer is full our runtime falls back to pausing generation, leading to long silent periods. This differs from prior stalls caused by internal worker eviction or KV cache locks.
investigation_notes: 15:30 Support: Asked customer for pcap and server-side socket stats — provided pcap showing repeated zero-window from client IP range.
15:55 SRE: Enabled extended write tracing on streaming-proxy for affected connections; confirmed kernel-level send buffer full before application-level backpressure rises.

16:20 Eng: Reproduced similar silence by throttling client ACKs in lab using tbf to simulate delayed-ack and small receive window; streaming runtime paused generation until socket became writable again.

17:10 Eng: Confirmed that our runtime currently blocks on send when kernel socket buffer is full. There is no aggressive application-level keepalive to push smaller chunks, and we don't currently surface a metric for socket-level zero-window occurrences.
17:45 Customer: Reported that affected users are behind a vendor NAT/gateway appliance with known aggressive receive-window management; vendor is investigating configuration for delayed ack settings.
actions_taken: Added temporary server-side application-heartbeat: streaming proxy will emit a 1-byte heartbeat frame every 8s when no tokens emitted for >6s (hotfix deployed to prod-us-east at 2026-03-06T03:10:00Z).
Increased socket send buffer and enabled non-blocking writes with EAGAIN handling in proxy write path (hotfix part 2 deployed 2026-03-06T04:00:00Z).
Instrumented and exported new metric proxy.socket_zero_window_count and runtime.socket_write_block_duration; dashboards created.
Opened PR to implement incremental-chunking of tokens and more aggressive keepalive and to surface backpressure to client SDKs (PR #4123).
resolution: Mitigated: Hotfixes (heartbeat + non-blocking write handling + buffer adjustments) reduced occurrences by ~92% for NovaHealth. Long-term fix in progress: merged PR #4123 implementing incremental-chunking and explicit backpressure signals to clients; scheduled rollout to all prod regions on 2026-03-10. Customer vendor confirmed they will relax delayed-ack settings for affected NAT appliance and monitor.
resolution_notes: Patch merged to main and staged to prod-us-east; monitoring shows residual incidents near 1-2% of sessions, primarily from legacy customer proxies still using small TCP receive windows. Follow-ups: (1) Add retry/fast-close protective logic if socket_write_block_duration > 30s, (2) Update developer docs to recommend client-side keepalives for long chat sessions, (3) Educate CS/SE on network-level troubleshooting steps.
